newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian parliament approves tv decree.
newsitem.headline: Italian parliament approves tv decree.

text.p: The Chamber of Deputies (lower house) approved a decree on Tuesday that would extend the broadcast licences of opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi's Mediaset company.
The decree, worked out in a deal between the government of Prime Minister Romano Prodi and the centre-right opposition, now moves on to the Senate.
It replaces an expiring decree which allowed Mediaset to carry on broadcasting its three terrestrial tv channels until the end of January.
Under the new decree, Mediaset's licences would be extended until the end of May.
The Constitutional Court ruled two years ago that no single proprietor should be allowed to keep three TV channels and set August 1996 as the deadline for changes to be implemented.

The government extended current ownership rules until the end of January 1997 after that deadline passed in order to plug a legal gap in which magistrates could technically have forced Berlusconi to take one of his channels off the air.
